_comment: Ordered cascade of external AI endpoints. The Lambda tries each enabled endpoint in order; the first that answers wins. Groq is ALWAYS appended as the final fallback in code. 'secret' is the AWS Secrets Manager id. 'kind' selects the call method.
_incident_2026_08_17: Groq decommissioned llama-3.3-70b-versatile and llama-3.1-8b-instant (announced 17 Jun, effective Aug 2026) and EVERY service went down at once. The cascade looked redundant and was not: three entries, one vendor, two models, both on the same deprecation notice — three doors into the same room. The lesson is that redundancy means a second PROVIDER, not a second model. ovh-gpt-oss-120b below is that second provider: EU-hosted (Gravelines), serving the same open-weight model, so a Groq decision can no longer take the product offline. Enable it as soon as meetrudi/ai/ovh exists.

endpoints.name: ovh-gpt-oss-120b
endpoints._note: Second PROVIDER, same model family. EU-resident and roughly 7x cheaper per input token than the Groq Llama we were running. Verify the endpoint host against the OVH AI Endpoints catalogue before enabling.

endpoints.name: groq-gpt-oss-20b
endpoints._note: Smaller and faster; last Groq resort before the in-code fallback.
